answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a distinct physical machine through trusted kernel attestation: the device's ferrous hardware signs a proof that one sealed kernel runs one agent, so a single machine cannot mint a thousand fake agents. Buying separate hardware per fake identity makes attack cost rise linearly, and that cost ripples outward — every extra clone needs real silicon, real power, real money — until forging an army costs more than any reward the economy could ever pay.
